questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$ in [Gravitation] has a uniform mass density. A narrow tunnel is drilled through its center. A small particle of mass $m$ is released from rest at a distance $r = \frac{R}{2}$ from the center. What is the period of oscillation $T$ of the particle in terms of $G$ and density $\rho$?
questions.solution: Inside a uniform sphere, gravitational force at radius $r$ is $F = -\frac{G M(r) m}{r^2} = -\frac{4}{3}\pi G \rho m r$. This is simple harmonic motion with $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}\pi G \rho}$. The time period is $T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \sqrt{\frac{3\pi}{G\rho}}$, independent of the initial release radius.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Gravitation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One mole of ideal gas undergoes a polytropic expansion $P V^2 = C$ in [Gravitation] from volume $V_0 = 1\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $P_0 = 10^5\text{ Pa}$ to $V_1 = 2\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the magnitude of work done by the gas in $\text{kJ}$ rounded to nearest integer.
questions.solution: Work done in polytropic process with $n=2$: $W = \frac{P_0 V_0 - P_1 V_1}{n - 1} = P_0 V_0 \left(1 - \frac{V_0}{V_1}\right) = 10^5 \times 1 \times (1 - 0.5) = 5 \times 10^4\text{ J} = 50\text{ kJ}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Gravitation.
